title: A Phase 1b/2 Trial of HER3-DXd with T-DXd in Participants with Hormone Receptor Positive, HER2-low or HER2-ultralow, Unresectable or metastatic BC
official: A Phase 1b/2, Multicenter, Open-label, Dose Regimen Determination and Dose Expansion Trial to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Anti-tumor Activity, and an Optimal Dose Regimen of Patritumab Deruxtecan (HER3-DXd) with Trastuzumab Deruxtecan (T-DXd) in Participants with Hormone Receptor Positive, HER2-low or HER2-ultralow, Unresectable or Metastatic Breast Cancer (HERTHENA-Breast02)
summary:
Main objective: 1. Arms 1 and 2: To assess the safety and tolerability of HER3-DXd and T-DXd
2. Arms 3 and 4: To assess the anti-tumor activity of HER3-DXd and T-DXd
conditions: HR+, HER2-low or HER2-ultralow, unresectable or mBC

interventions.name: Enhertu 100 mg powder for concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Sign and date the Informed Consent Form (ICF) prior to the start of any trial-specific qualification procedures. A separate Tissue Screening consent will be obtained from all participants before pretreatment tumor tissue collection to meet the baseline tumor tissue requirement.
2. 10. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0 or 1 at the time of Screening.
3. 11. Has ≥1 measurable lesion on computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as per RECIST v1.1 by investigator assessment.
4. 12. Has adequate bone marrow reserve and organ function based on local laboratory data within 7 days prior to the first dose as specified in the study protocol.
5. 13. A female participant of childbearing potential, as defined in Section 10.3.5 of the study protocol, is eligible to participate if the conditions specified in the study protocol are met.
6. 14. A male participant capable of producing sperm is eligible to participate if he agrees to the conditions specified in the study protocol during the intervention period and for at least the time needed to eliminate the trial intervention. The length of time required to continue contraception after the last dose for the trial intervention is 4 months.
7. 15. Is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, drug administration plan, laboratory tests, other trial procedures, and trial restrictions.
8. 2. Adults ≥18 years of age on the day of signing the ICF. Follow local regulatory requirements if the legal age of consent for trial participation is >18 years old.
9. 3. Pathologically documented breast cancer as per definition in the study protocol.
10. 4. Provides a pretreatment tumor tissue sample that meets the criteria specified in the study protocol
11. 5. Documented radiologic progression as per investigator assessment per RECIST v1.1 criteria (during or after most recent treatment).
12. 6. Documented refractoriness to endocrine therapy as specified in the study protocol.
13. 7. Prior treatment with a CDK4/6 inhibitor in any setting. Subsequent endocrine therapies administered after progression on CDK4/6 inhibitor are allowed.
14. 8. Participants with genomic alterations/mutations (PIK3CA, PTEN, AKT, or BRCA1/2) who are eligible for approved targeted therapies in combination with endocrine therapy or as monotherapy (according to local label and availability) must have received the corresponding therapy prior to enrollment, unless contraindicated or not accessible in their country/region.
15. 9. No prior chemotherapy for unresectable or metastatic breast cancer. Participants who have received chemotherapy in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant setting are eligible.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Prior treatment with an anti-HER3 antibody and/or ADC that consists of a topoisomerase I inhibitor (eg, T-DXd) or any topoisomerase I inhibitor therapy.
2. 10. Exposure to prior systemic anticancer therapy (including investigational agents) within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives (whichever is shorter) before randomization.
3. 11. Inadequate washout period before randomization, as defined in the study protocol.
4. 12. Uncontrolled or significant cardiovascular disease as defined in the study protocol.
5. 13. Has active or uncontrolled hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Hepatitis B screening testing is required. For further information please refer to the study protocol.
6. 14. Has active or uncontrolled hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. Hepatitis C screening testing is required. For further information please refer to the study protocol.
7. 15. Has active or uncontrolled human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. Participants must be tested for HIV viral load during the Screening Period if acceptable by local regulations or institutional review boards (IRBs)/independent ethics committees (IECs). For further information please refer to the study protocol.
8. 16. Has history of other active malignancy within 3 years prior to randomization, with exceptions specified in the study protocol.
9. 17. Has unresolved toxicities from previous anticancer therapy, defined as toxicities (other than alopecia) not yet resolved to National Cancer Institute-Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0 (NCI-CTCAE v5.0), Grade ≤1 or baseline. For further information please refer to the study protocol.
10. 18. Any known contraindication to treatment, including hypersensitivity to either the drug substances or inactive ingredients in the drug products.
11. 19. Evidence of ongoing uncontrolled systemic bacterial, fungal, or viral infection. Note: Participants with localized fungal infections of skin or nails are eligible.
12. 2. Has any history of interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis irrespective of steroid use, or current ILD, or suspected ILD, or ILD that cannot be ruled out by imaging at Screening.
13. 20. Psychological, social, familial, or geographical factors that would prevent regular follow-up.
14. 3. Has clinically severe respiratory compromise (based on the investigator’s assessment) resulting from intercurrent pulmonary illnesses as described in the protocol.
15. 4. Is receiving chronic systemic corticosteroids dosed at >10 mg daily prednisone or equivalent anti-inflammatory activity or any form of immunosuppressive therapy prior to randomization. Participants who require use of bronchodilators, inhaled or topical steroids, or local steroid injections may be included in the trial.
16. 5. Evidence of any leptomeningeal disease.
17. 6. Evidence of spinal cord compression or brain metastases, defined as being clinically active and symptomatic, or requiring therapy with corticosteroids or anticonvulsants to control associated symptoms. Participants with clinically inactive or treated brain metastases who are asymptomatic (ie, without neurologic signs or symptoms and do not require treatment with corticosteroids or anticonvulsants) may be included in the trial but must have a stable neurologic status for ≥4 weeks prior to Cycle 1 Day 1. Participants with asymptomatic brain metastases and treated with anticonvulsants as prophylaxis can enroll.
18. 7. Has clinically significant corneal disease.
19. 8. Any evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases (eg, active bleeding diatheses, active infection), psychiatric illness/social situations, geographical factors, substance abuse, or other factors that, in the investigator’s opinion, makes it undesirable for the participant to participate in the trial or that would jeopardize compliance with the protocol. Screening for chronic conditions is not required for eligibility.
20. 9. Prior or ongoing clinically relevant illness, medical condition, surgical history, physical finding, or laboratory abnormality that, in the investigator’s judgment, could affect the safety of the participant; alter the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of the trial intervention; or confound the assessment of trial results.
